Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; automation levers: Parcel screening; Comparable-sale tracking; key risks: Illiquidity; No legal access; Environmental constraints; regulatory notes: Review zoning, title, disclosures and broker licensing when representing others.; track ids: track_1; track_2; track labels: Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; Grey-Zone Growth & Traffic Arbitrage; plays: id: gis_landlocked_parcel_easement_assemblage; track id: track_1; name: GIS Landlocked-Parcel Spite-Strip & Access-Easement Assemblage Arbitrage; mechanism: Combine GIS parcel geometry with recorded access rights to option overlooked strips and negotiate voluntary easement assemblages; mapped boundaries alone do not establish legal access.; inputs: County GIS parcel and road layers; Recorded plats, deeds, and easement instruments; Surveyor estimates and neighboring-owner demand; workflow: 1. Flag apparently landlocked parcels and narrow connecting strips in GIS; 2. Verify boundaries, existing rights, and easement-by-necessity exposure with surveyor and counsel; 3. Secure contingent options and negotiate voluntary access agreements without obstructing existing access; 4. Record approved easements and close the assembled sale through title escrow; metrics: Verified access gaps per screened parcel; Option-to-recorded-easement conversion rate; Net assemblage margin after survey and title costs; platform risks: failure mode: GIS false positive or unenforceable access premium; trigger: Unmapped easement, boundary error, or preexisting legal right of access; impact: Option expiry or acquisition with no incremental assemblage value; detection metric: Survey and title exceptions per shortlisted parcel; fallback: Exercise diligence contingencies and offer survey-backed voluntary access services instead; id: forced_pooling_mineral_lease_curve_jumping; track id: track_1; name: Forced-Pooling Docket & Non-Consent Mineral Lease Curve-Jumping Arbitrage; mechanism: Use public pooling applications and drilling schedules to identify unleased mineral interests before election deadlines, pricing royalty upside against title defects and non-consent cost exposure.; inputs: State pooling dockets and election orders; Mineral ownership chain and lease abstracts; Operator development plans and local lease comparables; workflow: 1. Monitor pooling applications and map affected mineral tracts and hearing dates; 2. Verify net mineral acres, ownership authority, and election consequences with specialist counsel; 3. Negotiate disclosed lease or option terms and fund obligations before applicable deadlines; 4. Assign permitted interests or administer royalty receipts with division-order reconciliation; metrics: Verified net mineral acres acquired; Election deadlines met (%); Net royalty or assignment proceeds per invested dollar; platform risks: failure mode: Missed election or unexpected non-consent penalty; trigger: Stale docket feed or misread state-specific pooling order; impact: Delayed royalties and unbudgeted development-cost exposure; detection metric: Unverified order changes and days remaining to election; fallback: Stop acquisitions pending counsel review and choose only timely, fully understood permitted elections; id: fractional_heir_share_partition_forcing; track id: track_1; name: Fractional Heir-Share Acquisition & Tenancy-in-Common Partition Buyout Forcing; mechanism: Acquire documented fractional heir interests at a discount reflecting illiquidity, then seek consensual buyouts or counsel-supervised partition subject to heirs-property protections and co-owner rights.; inputs: Probate files and verified heirship records; Title chain, occupancy facts, and independent appraisal; Applicable partition and heirs-property protection rules; workflow: 1. Establish ownership fractions, probate authority, and encumbrances before contacting sellers; 2. Provide transparent offers with independent-advice opportunity and modeled partition costs; 3. Seek voluntary co-owner buyouts or an agreed market sale before considering litigation; 4. If unresolved, use counsel-led statutory procedures honoring notice, appraisal, and buyout rights; metrics: Verified ownership share acquired; Consensual resolution rate; Net proceeds after carrying and legal costs; platform risks: failure mode: Heirs-property protections defeat assumed forced-sale economics; trigger: Mandatory co-owner buyout, partition-in-kind preference, or defective heirship; impact: Long holding period and lower realizable value; detection metric: Unresolved heirs and statutory buyout conditions per property; fallback: Renegotiate voluntary exits or retain the interest without threatening unavailable remedies; id: cell_tower_billboard_easement_strip_out; track id: track_1; name: Cell-Tower, Rooftop & Billboard Perpetual Easement Strip-Out Arbitrage; mechanism: Separate assignable site-access and rent rights from underlying real estate for specialist buyers, pricing tenant termination rights and the permanent burden left on the residual property.; inputs: Tower, rooftop, and billboard leases and amendments; Title, lender consent, and zoning documents; Specialist easement-buyer bids and residual property appraisals; workflow: 1. Identify leased sites and reconcile actual rent receipts with termination and renewal terms; 2. Verify assignment rights, mortgage restrictions, maintenance duties, and required consents; 3. Compare easement sale proceeds against lost rent and residual property impairment; 4. Close approved conveyances through escrow and record access, utilities, and rent-allocation rights; metrics: Net easement proceeds versus retained rent value; Residual property value impairment; Consent-to-close cycle days; platform risks: failure mode: Nonassignable lease or excessive permanent property burden; trigger: Missing tenant or lender consent or easement scope exceeding valued rights; impact: Failed closing or reduced refinancing and resale value; detection metric: Unresolved consent conditions and residual appraisal discount; fallback: Retain the lease or negotiate a narrower term-limited assignment with all required approvals; id: ferc_grid_interconnection_queue_land_speculation; track id: track_1; name: FERC / ISO Substation Interconnection Queue & Powered-Land Option Flipping; mechanism: Overlay public interconnection queues with land-use and substation data to option potentially useful sites, treating queue position and nearby infrastructure as signals rather than guaranteed deliverable power.; inputs: ISO and utility interconnection queues and study results; Parcel zoning, transmission corridors, and substation maps; Utility service estimates and developer site requirements; workflow: 1. Match queue activity and infrastructure constraints to suitable parcels; 2. Verify site control requirements, zoning, environmental limits, and utility capacity assumptions; 3. Negotiate assignable diligence-contingent options within capped carrying-cost budgets; 4. Assign approved options to qualified developers with explicit disclosure of unresolved power and study conditions; metrics: Option cost per qualified developable acre; Utility-validated capacity versus marketed capacity; Net assignment proceeds after study and option costs; platform risks: failure mode: Queue withdrawal or prohibitive network upgrade cost; trigger: Restudy, milestone failure, or capacity estimate unsupported by utility commitments; impact: Option expiry and unrecoverable diligence spending; detection metric: Study cost revisions and unresolved interconnection milestones; fallback: Let contingent options lapse or reposition land for independently viable uses without claiming secured power; id: tcpa_litigator_scrub_honeypot_arbitrage; track id: track_2; name: TCPA Serial-Plaintiff Docket Scraping & Real-Time Litigator-Scrub Firewall Tollbooth; mechanism: Offer consent-first outbound compliance screening using lawful docket-derived risk signals alongside mandatory do-not-call and revocation checks; plaintiff matching neither authorizes contact nor replaces TCPA compliance.; inputs: Permitted public docket data with identity confidence scores; Consent provenance, revocations, and suppression lists; Applicable calling rules and customer retention policies; workflow: 1. Ingest permitted docket records with source dates, minimization, and human identity review; 2. Check consent, do-not-call status, revocations, and calling restrictions before optional risk enrichment; 3. Suppress noncompliant contacts and route uncertain matches to review without planting honeypots or provoking claims; 4. Serve auditable screening decisions with correction, deletion, and retention controls; metrics: Contacts blocked for missing consent or suppression match; False-positive identity match rate; Screening latency and stale-record share; platform risks: failure mode: False identity match or false assurance of permission to call; trigger: Stale docket data or treating absence from a plaintiff list as consent; impact: Unlawful outreach, privacy complaints, and customer liability; detection metric: Consent-audit failure rate and upheld identity correction requests; fallback: Disable uncertain enrichment and require independently verified consent and authoritative suppression checks; platform risks: failure mode: GIS false positive or unenforceable access premium; trigger: Unmapped easement, boundary error, or preexisting legal right of access; impact: Option expiry or acquisition with no incremental assemblage value; detection metric: Survey and title exceptions per shortlisted parcel; fallback: Exercise diligence contingencies and offer survey-backed voluntary access services instead; play id: gis_landlocked_parcel_easement_assemblage;
